commits.subject: ui: pdf - a GDI path is painted under the clip and with the pen of its painting record
commits.body:
GDI paints a path under the clip selected when StrokePath or FillPath runs. The renderer wrote the path's operators as the records came. A clip changed in between could only apply after the painting, and the pen's w, RG and d came inside the path object.

How it works now:
- From EMR_BEGINPATH to EMR_ENDPATH, only the records of the path's geometry (moves, lines, curves, shapes, EMR_CLOSEFIGURE) write to a stream of their own.
- Everything else goes to the page as it comes: clips, pen operators, text, bitmaps and the miter limit.
- The painting records end what the page left open, set the pen and the brush, write the kept path, then paint.
- EMR_ABORTPATH, EMR_SELECTCLIPPATH and the end of the metafile drop the path.

Fixed on the way (they broke paths before too):
- Text or a bitmap in a path bracket made the next line stroke the half-built path.
- A pen selected inside a path bracket stroked the pending line, an S with no path on the page.
- Arc, pie, chord, polygons, polylines, rectangles and ellipses painted at once inside a path, and the painting record painted them again.
- A polygon with a null pen and brush was left out of the path.
- FILLPATH filled with f under ALTERNATE.
- STROKEANDFILLPATH did not close the open figures.
- The Q after a clipped text forgot only the fill colour, while its underline had set the pen. TPdfEnum.GStateRestored now resets all four cached values, from TextOut and from SelectClip.

Still open:
- Text in a path: GDI adds its outlines to the path, the renderer draws it at once.
- Lines of a null pen outside a path leave their m l open on the page.

Tests: EmfClipRestoreDC has 9 more checks and EmfUnderlineClipped is new (2 checks); 10 of the new checks fail before.

This is the same change as in our engine (martin-doyle/mORMot2-PDF-CrossPlatform#94), without the path artifacts of tagged output, which this unit does not write.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - EMR_RESTOREDC restores the clip of EMR_EXTSELECTCLIPRGN, q and Q balanced
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - a stock font reads its bytes in the code page of its own charset
commits.body: EMR_EXTTEXTOUTA after a stock font decoded its bytes in CP_ACP (CP_OEMCP for OEM_FIXED_FONT), though ANSI_FIXED_FONT and ANSI_VAR_FONT are ANSI_CHARSET, cp1252, and the system fonts follow the system charset. The stock font's charset is now read with GetObjectW (CP_ACP if it gives none, or if the index is no font) and mapped as the charset of a selected font, by the new FontCharSetCodePage and StockFontCodePage. Measured here (code page 1252, OEM 850): lfCharSet 255 for OEM_FIXED_FONT, 0 for the others. The decoded text differs only where the system code page is not 1252; test EmfStockCodePages checks the code pages, and fails before. Found by Martin Doyle in our engine, where the same change is.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - the boxes of #686 under a mirrored axis
commits.body: With an axis mirrored, GDI records the box of Rectangle, Ellipse and RoundRect(100, 100, 500, 500) as 500,100,110,490 at 10 units per pixel: the recorded right is the smaller value. BoxInclI and RoundRectI normalized first and added the device pixel to the other side, so the shape moved by one pixel. DevPixelX/Y are signed now and the pixel goes to the recorded right/bottom before the box is normalized; RoundRectI passes its corners as TPdfCanvas.RoundRect wants them, and EMR_ROUNDRECT no longer normalizes the record in place. Not changed: under a world scale the pixel is not divided by the world factor - the record holds integer logical units, what GDI rounds to is not measured yet. Test EmfMirroredBoxes.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - EMR_CREATEBRUSHINDIRECT and EMR_EXTCREATEPEN read in their EMF layout (FPC 3.2.2 on Win64)
commits.body: The windows unit of FPC 3.2.2 declares both records with the native LOGBRUSH and EXTLOGPEN, whose ULONG_PTR hatch moves the fields on Win64 (lbColor at offset 20 instead of 16): every brush and extended pen of a metafile was drawn black there. TPdfEnum reads them through its own TEmrCreateBrushIndirect32 and TEmrExtCreatePen32, as #687 does in mormot.lib.gdiplus. Test EmfRecordLayout (fails on FPC 3.2.2 Win64 only).
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - ReduceTTF reads within the subset and writes within its result (#673, row 22)
commits.body:
It checked SubSetSize against SizeOf(PTtfTableDirectory), the pointer instead of the 12-byte header, and none of the directory entries. Now the header and its entries must lie in the subset, each kept table in the subset and in the result, which is as long as the subset - entries sharing one table wrote past it - and a head must hold checkSumAdjustment; otherwise the subset is used as it is, as with fewer than eight kept tables. The binary search fields of the directory are computed from the number of tables: the fixed values were right for ten only.

ReduceTTF is not in the interface and FontSub's output is sane, so only the search fields are tested here: ReducedFontSearchFields embeds Mongolian Baiti, which has no 'cvt ' table, so its subset keeps nine. Our engine tests the bounds on the same code (TestReducedFontBounds).
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - a printer resolution of 0 is asked again, not divided by (#673, row 21)
commits.body: CurrentPrinterRes kept a resolution of 0 when CreateDC or GetDeviceCaps failed, and MM_ISOTROPIC divided by it; RenderMetaFile checked only its X. It keeps 300 dpi now, and RenderMetaFile asks again when either axis is 0 or less. CurrentPrinterRes and CurrentPrinterPaperSize passed GetProfileString a size in bytes, twice their buffer on Unicode compilers. Test EmfPrinterResZero.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - EMR_STRETCHDIBITS flips a copy of its header (#673, row 20)
commits.body: Under a flipped transform it negated biHeight inside the record, which EnumEnhMetaFile hands out as const: a second rendering of the same metafile drew the bitmap the other way round. It flips a copy of the header now (cbBmiSrc bytes, checked against the record size). The same goes for EMR_ROUNDRECT, which normalized its box in the record - see the mirrored boxes commit. Test EmfDIBitsKept.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - EMR_EXTTEXTOUTA reads its bytes in the code page of the font (#673, row 19)
commits.body: The A record went through the Unicode path, reading twice its bytes as WideChars. Its bytes are converted in the code page of the font's charset - CP_ACP for DEFAULT_CHARSET and for a stock font, CP_OEMCP for OEM_FIXED_FONT (selecting a stock font clears the font of the metafile) - glyph indexes are left as they are, and the per-byte dx is dropped when the character count differs. Windows records ExtTextOutA as EMR_EXTTEXTOUTW, so the tests build their A records from W ones: EmfAnsiText (ANSI, Greek and Shift-JIS) and EmfAnsiStockFont.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - a scaled rotation is drawn without ArcSin/ArcCos past 1 (#673, row 18)
commits.body: ScaleMatrix took ArcSin(eM12) and TextOut ArcCos(eM11): a rotation scaled by 2 gave them a value past 1 - EInvalidOp on Delphi, NaN on FPC, where 180-degree text then came out upright. The angle is ArcTan2(eM12, eM11) now. Test EmfScaledRotation.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - EMR_RESTOREDC restores the state it names, however deep (#673, row 17)
commits.body: RESTOREDC popped one state whatever its iRelative, and the 32 saved states were guarded by Assert only. The stack is a dynamic array grown by SaveDC (the "with DC[nDC]" of EnumEMFFunc is evaluated per record, so it stays valid); a restore of a state not saved is ignored, as GDI fails it. Test EmfRestoreDCDepth.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - the polylines of EMR_POLYPOLYLINE stay open (#673, row 16)
commits.body: Each polyline of EMR_POLYPOLYLINE and EMR_POLYPOLYLINE16 got a segment back to its first point; only the polygons are closed now. Test EmfPolyPolylineOpen.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - EMR_ALPHABLEND draws its bitmap opaque (#673, row 15)
commits.body: Its BLENDFUNCTION was passed to DrawBitmap as the transparent colour: with AC_SRC_OVER and a constant alpha of 255 ($00FF0000), every pure blue pixel became a hole. Constant and per-pixel alpha stay unsupported. Test EmfAlphaBlendOpaque.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - TPdfTtf reads the format 4 cmap within its table (#673, row 14)
commits.body:
Only the start of the subtable was checked. Now the bound is the table's own byte length (GetTtfData gives it through a new optional Size): a table shorter than its header, a directory of more records than it holds, or a format 4 header and arrays (segCountX2 * 4 + 2 bytes) past it is not read; a segment with startCode > endCode holds no code (it made the count negative, then later segments wrote past the arrays); a glyph read through idRangeOffset must lie in the table - an index before the glyph array, inside the table, stays as it was: GDI maps it so too.

No test: GDI refuses to load a face whose (3,1) cmap is broken in any of these ways (measured with AddFontMemResourceEx on a patched Tahoma), so the trunk cannot reach them through GDI - defensive, as row 14 says. Our engine gets the tables from FreeType too, and tests them there.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: test: ui pdf - the expected hash of the metafile rendered since #686
commits.body: #686 draws the rectangles and ellipses of a metafile one device pixel larger, as GDI records them. Diffing the PDF of MetafileRenderingAndOrientation before and after #686 shows only these boxes (the dots 6 pt wide instead of 4.5, a rectangle 405 x 196.5 pt instead of 403.5 x 195), so the expected hash was stale - it is checked on Delphi Win32 only, code page 1252.

commits.subject: gdiplus: EMR_CREATEBRUSHINDIRECT and EMR_EXTCREATEPEN read in their EMF layout (FPC 3.2.2 on Win64)
commits.body: The windows unit of FPC 3.2.2 declares both records with the native LOGBRUSH and EXTLOGPEN, whose ULONG_PTR hatch moves the fields on Win64: lb.lbColor is at offset 20 instead of 16, the elp fields 4 bytes off. Every brush was read black there. FPC trunk declares them with LOGBRUSH32 and EXTLOGPEN32, as Delphi does; the converter now reads them through its own TEmrCreateBrushIndirect32 and TEmrExtCreatePen32 on every compiler. Test EmfPlusRecordLayout.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: gdiplus: the window/viewport mapping, then the playback transform, without rounding
commits.body: Follow-up to #679. ScaleMatrix translated by ViewOrg * Win / View - WinOrg, rounded by MulDiv; a page point is at (p - WinOrg) * View / Win + ViewOrg, now in floating point, since the playback transform may scale it a lot. It also applied that playback transform - the one EnumEnhMetaFile sets on the target DC, mapping the metafile frame to the picture - before the mapping: GDI+ multiplies row vectors, so the order is now World x Map x Dest. Tests EmfPlusViewportOrigin, EmfPlusPlaybackOrder and EmfPlusWindowOrigin.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: gdiplus: a PS_NULL pen draws nothing
commits.body: Follow-up to #679: CreatePenObj made a solid GDI+ pen of the colour and width given for EMR_CREATEPEN and EMR_EXTCREATEPEN with PS_NULL; it now gets handle 0, as the stock NULL_PEN. Windows records CreatePen(PS_NULL) as the stock pen, so the test EmfPlusNullPen patches PS_NULL into the records of two solid pens.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: gdiplus: EMR_RESTOREDC restores the depth it names, and the saved clip under its own transform
commits.body: Follow-up to #679. TGdiplusEnum.RestoreDC popped one state whatever the record's iRelative, and set the saved clip region before restoring the transform: GdipGetClip gave that region under the transform of the saved state, so SAVEDC; MODIFYWORLDTRANSFORM scale 1/16; RESTOREDC left the clip at 1/16 of its size. It now drops -iRelative states (ignoring a state that was not saved, as GDI fails it), frees their regions, restores the transform, then the clip. The states are a dynamic array, grown by SaveDC, instead of 11 guarded by Assert. EnumerateEnd freed DC[nDC].ClipRegion nDC times instead of DC[i]. Tests EmfPlusClipRestored and EmfPlusRestoreDepth.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: orm: InBatchOfCurrentThread checks fBatchMethod within the storage lock
commits.body:
no unlocked read of fBatchMethod/fBatchThread
the BATCH owner keeps the (reentrant) storage lock from InternalBatchStart to InternalBatchStop, so it enters at once, whereas any other thread waits  for the BATCH to be sent: once the lock is acquired, fBatchMethod <> mNone  means that the current thread is the BATCH owner
commits.author: Dimitris Kounalakis

commits.subject: orm: fixed TRestStorageExternal regular writes from another thread during a BATCH
commits.body:
- EngineAdd/EngineUpdate/EngineDelete/EngineDeleteWhere did check fBatchMethod
  BEFORE taking the storage lock: while a thread was within its own
  InternalBatchStart/InternalBatchStop (which owns the lock), a regular write
  from ANOTHER thread on the same table did see this BATCH state
- e.g. a regular Update during a BATCH POST of another thread returned false
  at once, with no exception nor DB error; and with a matching method, the
  write was appended into the BATCH of the other thread, without the lock
- the BATCH owner thread is now stored in fBatchThread: only this thread uses
  the BATCH process, others follow the regular path, which waits for the
  storage lock, i.e. for the BATCH to be sent
- the regular path does not use fBatchOptions any more, which may belong to
  the BATCH of another thread (e.g. boInsertOrIgnore)
- added TTestExternalDatabase.BatchFromOtherThread regression test
commits.author: Dimitris Kounalakis
